creator: Chris Huber Reitz
name: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat — Directive on Automated Decision-Making
quote: The final decision must be made by a human. Decisions cannot be made without having clearly defined human involvement during the decision-making process. Humans review the decisions or recommendations made by the system for accuracy and appropriateness.
quote_label: Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Appendix C, Ensuring human involvement (s. 6.3.13), Level III (effective 2019-04-01; 2025 amendments; primary page read 2026-09-27)

provenance.note: Risk-tiered regime (Appendix B levels I-IV). Levels I-II: 'The system may make decisions and assessments without direct human involvement.' Levels III-IV (high / very high, 'difficult to reverse' / 'irreversible'): human makes the final decision. D1=2: publish the algorithmic impact assessment on the Open Government Portal before production (6.1.1); retain the right to 'access, test and monitor' proprietary components (6.2.6.1); document decisions (6.2.7); data 'traceable' (6.3.6). D2=2: a named ADM/senior official is responsible for every requirement; deputy-head approval to operate at levels III-IV (6.3.14). D3=2: 'Providing notice through all service delivery channels in use that the decision will be made or assisted by an automated decision system' (6.2.1) plus meaningful explanation after decisions (6.2.3). D4=0: no synthetic-identity or fabrication provision; 6.3.11 anti-tampering is about model integrity, not impersonation. D5=2: human final decision + review 'for accuracy and appropriateness' at III-IV; overrides documented (6.3.4). D6=2: pre-production testing 'for accuracy, unintended biases' (6.3.1), outcome monitoring (6.3.2), data validation (6.3.5), expert peer review published (6.3.7). c2_fit=partially: the permit/reserve line keys on impact and reversibility, not on whether the output is checkable. Reversibility is a proxy for verification economics (a reversible decision is corrected cheaply after the fact via recourse, 6.4) but the directive never asks how costly it is to prove a given output right. A clean case of a stakes-keyed rather than proof-keyed line.
